title: France becomes first European Union country to ban social media for kids under 15
facts: The French parliament approved legislation banning social media for children under 15 by a vote of 279 to 81.
France became the first country in the European Union to ban social media for children under the age of 15.
Children under 15 in France will be barred from creating new social media accounts starting in September.
Existing social media accounts belonging to children under 15 in France will be blocked starting in January 2027.
The French legislation prohibits students from having mobile phones in high schools starting next year.
Students in France were already banned from having mobile phones in elementary and middle schools.
The French law requires social media platforms to implement age verification checks.
The French legislation includes exemptions for educational platforms and online encyclopedias.
Australia became the first country in the world to ban under-16s from social media at the end of 2025.
A poll by Australia's internet regulator in March found approximately 70% of parents reported their children remained on social media despite the ban.
Maya Thomas serves as a legal and policy officer at the British organization Big Brother Watch.
The United Kingdom announced plans to introduce a ban on social media accounts for under-16s starting in January 2027.
France and Germany announced plans to develop an alternative to military software supplied by the US firm Palantir.
France's domestic intelligence service ended its contract with the tech firm Palantir earlier this year.
France is the second country worldwide to implement a nationwide social media ban for children.
